_source: Recorded by `bun run explain:probe:context-matrix 7.24.5` (scripts/probes/explain-context-matrix.ts) on stock CHR 7.24.5 x86, 2026-11-01 — two disposable CHRs (IP routes, MAC routes), 59 cells, every product cell through centrs executeEnvelope with pinned --via. Replicated on a second full-matrix pass with identical cell outcomes and gate table. Re-run that command to reproduce, then regenerate this file mechanically with `bun run explain:probe:context-matrix --slice <matrix-capture.json>` (cells/gate/inputs from the capture; routes/findings prose preserved for human review — a re-record that changes conclusions needs its prose and replay test updated too); per-run captures stay in `.scratch/`. Session submissions always carry their raw screen. Findings read per #507's dimensions; unknowns stay unknown. No router is needed to read this file.

rest.sessions: one /execute call per submission; fresh scope each call

native.sessions: one /execute call per submission; fresh scope each call

ssh.sessions: one ssh exec channel per submission

session.sessions: one held MacTelnetConsole per cell (login once, one run() per submission); no validation

stored.sessions: REST-created /system/script, one script per submission, run via product REST

inputs.intent: local/set/put across newlines: one scope or per-line scopes
same three statements joined by semicolons on one line
explicit braces around the three statements, one line
explicit braces with physical newlines inside (continuation)
global set in one submission, read in the next
menu navigation then print: context within vs across calls
leading BOM before a trivial command per route

findings: SUBMISSION-1: /execute over REST and native runs multiline input as ONE scope (I1/I4 whole -> a=2; I6 menu+print in one call shows the table). Stored scripts agree (a=2).

SUBMISSION-2: SSH command execution runs multiline input PER LINE: I1 whole over ssh answers `syntax error (line 1 column 6)` + `a=` (line 2 :set rejected in its own scope, line 3 :put sees nothing); I4 whole answers `missing closing brace (line 1 column 2)` + the same tail. Coordinates are per-line (line 1), not whole-input.

SUBMISSION-3: mac-telnet console runs multiline sends per line too: I1 whole shows the last line's echo plus `a=`. Braced multiline (I4) is absorbed as one submission on the console (`{... }` fold, a=2).

SUBMISSION-4: `;`-joined statements are one scope on EVERY route incl. the console: I2 answers a=2 on rest/native/ssh/stored, and the session raw screen shows the device printing a=2 (the product mac-telnet ret is empty — reader extraction loss, see DELIVERY-2).

SUBMISSION-5: a bare menu path is not executable over /execute (rest: routeros/request-failed `no such command`; native: routeros/api-trap) but navigates fine on console routes (ssh/mac/session/stored nav all ok). A bare `print` is validation/unknown-path on every product route (device stage; direct fallback confirms `bad command name print`) and routeros/unknown-path when run inside a stored script.

SUBMISSION-6: menu context holds WITHIN one submission on every route it runs on (I6 whole shows the 192.0.2.44 entry on rest/native/stored/mac/session). ACROSS submissions it holds only on a held console (I6 session split shows the table; stored split answers `bad command name print`).

SUBMISSION-7: ssh cannot carry multiline menu navigation: I6 whole over ssh exits 1 with no output (transport/network), reproduced 3/3 runs on separate CHRs while validation passed. Single-line nav over ssh is fine. Mechanism unknown; the transport/network code mislabels a device-side refusal — follow-up filed.
BODY-1: each stored-script run is one scope (I1-I4 whole -> a=2) and scripts share device-global state: a global set in one script reads g=11 in the next.
BODY-2: partial script input is never final state, but globals cross every submission boundary measured: g=11 reads back on rest/native/ssh/stored product calls and (raw screen) on the held console.

BODY-3: locals never leak across submissions anywhere: every split read shows empty (`a=`) or the middle :set is rejected (`syntax error (line 1 column 6)` — the validation/syntax on split middles matches device truth on all four product routes).

ENV-1 (unicode/BOM note from #507): rest/native/stored preserve non-ASCII end to end (ret `héllo→574`). The RouterOS console strips non-ASCII input bytes: the mac raw echo/output shows `hllo574`, and ssh ret is `hllo574` — one console-input mechanism, two routes.

ENV-2 (BOM): a leading BOM splits by device path, not by centrs: the offline stage passes (abstains) on every route; REST/native device :parse rejects (validation/syntax; direct fallback `expected command name (line 1 column 1)`); console :parse accepts and runs (ssh/mac ret `bom574`); a stored script carrying a BOM fails at run (`expected command name (line 1 column 1)`).

GATE-1 (identity/permissions dimension): every scope-bearing shape is write-shaped in centrs — I1..I4, I5-set and script-run all need --yes (usage/confirmation-required); pure reads (I5-read, I7) run without. Valid syntax never implies executability: I6-nav passes validation and fails at the device.

DELIVERY-1: ssh multiline menu navigation is refused by the device channel (exit 1, silent) while the identical bytes work over the interactive console — a route delivery difference with its own follow-up.

DELIVERY-2: the mac-telnet console reader drops :put output for single-line sends with trailing newline and non-trivial content (I2/I3/I5-read/I7 ret/product-output empty while the committed raw screens show the device printing a=2, g=11, hllo574). Multiline sends leak echo artifacts into ret (a `[cmx@CHR] > :put ...` line; a `{... }` fold). Same reader, same follow-up — the product mac-telnet cells for I2/I3/I5/I7 are extraction artifacts, not device answers.
UNKNOWN-1: ssh multiline-nav exit-1 mechanism; console echo-shape switch behind DELIVERY-2; BOM-strip location in the console input path — recorded as unknown, not guessed.

UNKNOWN-2: cross-cell leakage on a long-held console (fresh console per cell by design); any RouterOS version other than 7.24.5 x86; SSH-interactive-shell (PTY) submission, which RouterOS does not grant over SSH.
